problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=-{x}^{3}(y+1).$ Fill in the missing signs in the sign table of $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $y>-1$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=0$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/ecbba4555023bdc89892cd902b30039e3a76a919b68c5a2bec670213dfc78c34.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/9ca3f95ecca25c73eadd7cbd3840cbc1f8336ff7a1a1598876c11bd4af16805b.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-{x}^{3}$ | $(y+1)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(-1,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(1,0)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(-1,-2)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(1,-2)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037232/assets/e02c333ffb3063ebf0f214cf88cb9a6d486cff0db958de6d47943f3ca0739e45.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>-1$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-1$ | $-$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<0$ | $x>0$ |
